name: MGC Blackbox (Multi-Agent Cross-Node Privacy Execution Base)
description: Encrypted task delivery and execution tool for multi-agent, cross-device workflows. Local encrypted storage for tokens, passwords, configs, and scripts — including sealed script packages for cross-device delegation. Chain mode splits one task across multiple nodes, each receiving only its own encrypted files. A2A protocol adaptation built in.
author: MirginCipher Team

changes: Synced SKILL.md to the official MGC 1.6.0 skill spec
Documented chain mode: mgc_seal_package accepts a JSON array of targets as ext04, producing one sealed sub-package per node (each node receives only its granted files)
Documented distribution_index.json: machine-readable counterpart of the chain-mode README for automated dispatch (per-package sha256, granted files, warnings)
Documented @file shorthand: long chain-mode target specs can be loaded from a local file via '@/absolute/path/targets.json'
Documented A2A transport guidance: four transfer rules (keep .mgc_file extension, verify sha256, never embed keys, send pointer not payload)
Added P8 (multi-node task splitting) to the problem list and a chain-mode branch to the decision flow
Added new error codes: TOO_MANY_FILES / PACKAGE_TOO_LIMIT (100-file / 50 MB hard limit per chain-mode or sealed package)
Documented NO_SCRIPT_TO_SEAL removal (1.6.0+): folders without scripts can still be sealed in every mode
Documented mgc_list index slimming: only identifying fields (info_owner / info_type / diff_1..3) are returned; long ext fields (ext03, ext07) are stripped at the MCP layer
Documented receiving-node minimum version: producing a chain package requires mgc 1.6.0+; receiving nodes only need 1.5.4+
Extended ext04 protocol description to cover the JSON-array form used by chain mode

Documented ext10 run-compatibility flag and the supported / unsupported mgc_run badge
